institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted a change of scenery.
And I wanted to try living in another country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great time!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
generally information was easy to find on the website of the university.
But when something more challenging came up, i was thrown around between people and departments. I had to show up at different information desks, offices and, send emails, call people before it was finally solved.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I showed up at meetings for international students, showed up at help desks, got email responses and had phonecalls.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was sometimes difficult to know exactly where to go for questions. The chemistry department was better at helping than the international office.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Nordic students are not able to find housing via the university (SIT)
So look for acommodation early on
Hybel.no
It is way cheaper to live with a few other students in a shared house or apartment than living in the apartments owned by private companys.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in an apartment owned by campusliving. It seems that they place international students together, so if you would like to live with norwegians, this might not be the best option

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
When renting in Trondheim, most leases go from july-june, and there is no option to get out of the lease.
I paid way more for the same room because i signed a short lease (6 months) 
Be aware that a lot of international students sign a cheaper lease, that is binding for a year. so a lot of people are desperate to have other people take over their lease for the spring semester. I saw several people offering their lease to other studens cheaper than the actual rent, to get out of their lease.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: if you want to take courses that have some requirements, this might take som time to get approved by NTNU.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You register online at 'studentweb'
you are able to register for more courses than you would like to actually take.
it is your own responsibility to make sure that timeplans doesnt overlap, and exams arent at the same time.
you can take new courses until the 15th of september
you can withdraw from an exam until 2 weeks before

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
you can find information on 'Innsida' and
NTNU.no

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I had to make changes because timetables did not align.
I had a hard time registering for KJ2031, but after being persistant it worked out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: do your research before orientation week, so you have a plan A, B and C if timetables do not align or the courses arent what you expect

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Quite similar
But the instructors that help with hand-ins were not as approachable as im used to, so I ususally did not talk to them even though I was there.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
INTRO175 - Introduction to Norway (english)
KJ2031 - Videregående uorganisk kjemi (norwegian)
TMT4186 - Materialkjemi (norwegian)
TMT4320 - Nanomaterials (English)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you liked kemiKS, KJ2031 gives another perspective to molecular orbitals and such. very sweet professor.
If you want more materials chemistry TMT4186 has a very different perspective than the course at UCPH. There was no talk of magnetism but a lot of time spend on mechanic properties. quite large curriculum.

TMT4320 had some quite hard hand-ins, but the final exam was not as hard. a lot of techniques to remember. The book was expensive, but they have one copy at the library. you are only allowed to read it at the library, but it worked.

INTRO175 was very intersting if you want to learn about norwegian history, language and culture. large curriculum and the books are expensive.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I am used to biking in copenhagen, so having to rely on and pay for public transportation was unexpected.
Getting settled cost more than expected. I had to buy a topmattress, and stuff like that for my room to be livable.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: coffee is not as expensive as it is in Copenhagen. At university (at SIT cafe) a barista cappucino cost about 22 DKK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
NTNU has very big sports organisation NTNUI with nearly every sport possible.
In Trondheim there is a big student community at Studenter Samfundet
Every study program has a 'linjeforening' where students get together and do different activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Join a sport at NTNUI. I am not sporty so I volunteered at Studenter Samfundet instead. I did this to meet Norwegians and not only other international students. I volunteered in 'bargjengen' which is a part of 'kafe- og serveringsgjengen'
highly recommend!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to a concert, a quiz or just party at studentersamfundet. There is a quiz on tuesdays, music quiz on fridays, and wednesday is wine wednesday.
Nature is close in Trondheim, but more easily accesible in the summertime, so go on hikes in bymarka when the weather is at its best

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Norwegians and danes are alike, so you quickly adjust. But this also means that you notice the small things.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
join a club or volunteer. 
Norwegians are usually the most open to new people, when they have a beer in hand

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: light switches are opposite, so I kept leaving the light on because the switch looked on.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: everything being closed on sundays. I liked that sundays where for going for a hike, a swim in the fjord or just being cozy at home.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Register for more courses than you plan on taking

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The welcome week is not like at UCPH, so set your expectations low

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a breath of fresh air

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: navigating the system. sometimes you are floating between two institutions, and it is difficult to know whether to contact ucph or ntnu.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
